lines: // The pop-out page's composition root (kb:adr/reader-popout-is-a-second-page) — a second
// Vite entry, not a hash route inside `index.html`'s own composition root. Builds the same
// `App` + `WsClient` shape `main.ts` does; there is no masthead, rail, banner or any other
// feature here. `mountStandaloneReader` (features/reader.ts) owns finding `#reader-host`,
// choosing the unknown-session notice over a real reader, and mounting the reader's root —
// this module only builds `app`, registers the reader/theme/update-restart/connection
// controllers and the client, and starts the tick.
// `onSessionRemoved`/`onUsage`/`onShellActivity`/`onProtocolMismatch` are deliberately not
// wired — no feature on this page reads any of them — but `onUpdate`/`onHelloArrived` are
// (`popoutWsHandlers`, wsapp.ts), so an open pop-out reloads after an update restart like the
// dashboard. It has no banner, so the restart banner and `Updated to` confirmation go unread.
keeps.reason: Edited on `main`; still true: `popoutWsHandlers(app, connection)` registers the update handlers and the file builds the reader, theme, update-restart and connection controllers it describes.

lines: // The line says the daemon was unreachable, which stops being true at the next hello; a

keeps.reason: Without it a reader would make the helloArrived handler clear the action-error line unconditionally; that would wipe refusals and partial batch reports at `if (shownMessage === networkError.message) showActionError(null);`.

lines: /** The pop-out's handler set: `coreWsHandlers` plus the update-restart signals, so an open
* pop-out reloads onto the new version like every dashboard window. */
// xterm sizes the alternate buffer's line list from these rows when it is built and
// only ever grows it while that buffer is still empty; starting at the minimum lets
// the first fit grow it to exactly the fitted rows, so a shrink from the 24-row
// default never leaves the buffer a scroll range that eats the first wheel event.
keeps.reason: Without it a reader would raise `rows: 2` to a normal size or drop it as an arbitrary magic number; that gives the alternate buffer a scroll range that eats the first wheel event at `rows: 2,`.

lines: // spawn runs run on m.runCtx, tracked on m.wg so Stop cancels and waits for it. Once Stop
// has begun it starts nothing, so a late caller (an Apply arriving during shutdown) never
// adds to a WaitGroup Stop is already waiting on.
// Stop cancels the poll loop and any SessionEnd pane watch and waits for them to exit,
// giving up when ctx is done. Also flags checkOneLiveness's opportunistic callers (see the
// stopped field doc) to stop persisting — set first, so it takes effect for a Nudge racing
// this call regardless of how long the wait below takes.
// runCtx is the lifetime of every goroutine the Manager starts (spawn); Stop cancels it
// and waits on wg. Written once by NewManager; spawnMu orders spawn's wg.Add against
// Stop's flip of stopped, so no Add can race Stop's Wait.
